transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, thank you. I'm here because... my head just feels really foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things. Like, um, appointment times, or the dates for the exhibits I help out with. I'll even forget which volunteer I already called on the phone and end up calling them twice. It's just been very frustrating to not be able to think clearly, so I thought I should come in.
When did you first notice this fogginess and forgetfulness?

I'd say... it's been about four months now. It started right around the time we had some water damage at the house. That ended up pushing us into having to do a remodel, and... well, that's when I really started noticing it.
Have these memory and thinking problems made it harder for you to manage your usual daily activities independently?

Yes, it really has. I mean, I've actually missed a couple of my own doctor visits. And I tangled up the schedule at the senior center so badly that... well, my husband has had to step in. He's been helping me with all the phone calls and keeping the calendar straight now. He even had to take over making the decisions for the house repairs, which is something I always used to handle myself. It's just been too hard to keep it all straight on my own lately.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days lately?
No, not really. I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or down. It's just the memory issues and the fogginess that have been bothering me.
{"intent":"Clarify whether the cognitive decline is progressive","question":"Since you first noticed these problems, have they been steadily getting worse?""}

I'm not really sure if it's getting worse, to be honest. It's... well, it's hard to tell. It feels like ever since it started a few months ago, my memory has just been stuck this way. I haven't really noticed it going downhill day by day or anything like that. It's just been a constant problem since all that house stuff happened.
Has your husband or anyone else close to you noticed and commented on changes in your memory or thinking?

Well, I don't know if he's said anything specific about it getting worse, but he definitely knows I'm struggling. I mean, he wouldn't have taken over the calendar and the house stuff if he didn't notice I was having trouble. He hasn't sat me down and said, "Your memory is bad," but his actions kind of show he sees it.
Have you had any formal memory or thinking tests with a healthcare professional that showed a decline from your previous abilities?
No, I haven't had any tests like that. Um, no one has made me take a memory test or sit down with a doctor to check it. This is really the first time I'm talking to a professional about it.
Before these problems began, were you able to manage your appointments, phone calls, and household decisions independently without difficulty?

Oh, yes. I used to do all of that without any trouble. I always kept track of things. But... well, lately, I've missed doctor visits, and I got the senior center schedule completely tangled up. It got so bad that my husband had to step in. Now he helps with the phone calls and keeps the calendar straight. He even has to handle the repair decisions for the house, which I always used to just take care of myself.
Would you be willing to complete a brief memory and thinking test today?
Well, yes, I suppose that would be fine. If you think it will help us figure out what's going on with me, I don't mind taking a test today. I'm right here, so we might as well.
Please repeat these three words: apple, table, penny.
Apple, table, penny.
What were the three words I asked you to remember?
Oh... let me think. I know I just said them a moment ago. But... no, I'm sorry. They've completely slipped my mind. I honestly can't remember what they were right now.
Are you unable to manage your appointments, phone calls, and household decisions on your own now, or does your husband mainly help as a precaution?

Well, no, it's not really just a precaution anymore. I genuinely can't manage them. I've missed doctor visits, and... well, I tangled up my schedule at the senior center so badly recently. My husband has just had to step in and take over. He helps with all the phone calls, keeping the calendars straight, and even making decisions about repairs around the house. I always used to handle all those things myself, but I just can't seem to keep it all straight right now.
Has your husband noticed that your memory or thinking is clearly worse than it was before these problems began?

Yes, he definitely has. In fact, that's exactly what brought me in to see you. My head just feels... foggy. I keep mixing up simple things that I used to handle just fine. Things like appointment times, exhibit dates, or even forgetting which volunteer I already called for an event. He sees it happening, and... well, it's very clear to both of us that my thinking is just worse than it was before all this started.
Do you need your husband to take over any activities that you previously managed independently because of your memory or thinking problems?

Well, like I was just saying a moment ago, yes. He's had to take over the phone calls, the schedules, and the decisions around the house. I used to do all of that independently before my memory got like this. But besides the things we just talked about... no, I can't really think of anything else he's had to step in for. That's really the main bulk of it.
